questions.q: What does the rule of thumb 'native first, escalate on evidence' mean?
options: Always buy an external tool for any dashboard
Never use anything except native reports
Build natively, and move only when a specific requirement native can't meet justifies the cost
Escalate as soon as any stakeholder asks for a chart
questions.explain: Default to native and escalate only when you can name a specific unmet requirement that the business cares enough about to pay for.

questions.q: Which is the FIRST of the five questions to ask about a reporting need?
options: Can one report type plus filters answer it?
Which vendor has the best demo?
How many licenses can we afford?
Does the CEO like the color scheme?
questions.explain: Most operational questions are answered by a single report type and filters, so check that first before considering any other tool.

questions.q: A VP wants Salesforce pipeline combined with monthly ERP revenue. Which question does this fail natively?
options: Whether the report can be filtered by date
Whether the report has a chart
Whether the dashboard can be scheduled
Whether the data comes from outside Salesforce
questions.explain: Native reports only use data in Salesforce, so blending ERP revenue requires an approach that can bring outside data in.

questions.q: Why is 'two versions of the truth' listed as a hidden cost of going external?
options: External tools cannot display numbers
Salesforce forbids exporting data
A native number and an external number that disagree destroy stakeholder trust
It only happens with Tableau
questions.explain: When two tools report different values for the same metric, people stop trusting either, which costs more than the original limitation.

questions.q: Why should you confirm current details before recommending a specific analytics product?
options: Product names, packaging, and licensing change often, so recommendations from memory can be wrong
Salesforce does not sell analytics products
Analytics products never change
Recommendations are illegal without a contract
questions.explain: Salesforce analytics products, names, and licensing evolve frequently, so verify current capabilities and pricing first.
